items.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: Now the guy that plays with the Basie band now, I think his name is T.J., he is very good at what he does too.

ctx.x: Now see, when I got a chance to work with Basie, Freddie was still around, but Basie wasn’t playing anymore, because he was kind of sick. But by working with the band all the other guys were still there. And Freddie Green came through, I was working in Chicago with Joe. And he came after their show and sat down and listened to us. And he came up to me. I knew who he was, but I didn’t think he knew who I was. And he came up to me and he really enjoyed my guitar playing. So we became friends. And I always asked…

But the style that, when I first saw the Basie band, Freddie’s style was more felt than heard, you know? And when you listened for it you could hear it. Because it was like the pulse of the band. It was pumping the band all of the time. And at any time that you could decipher each instrument, you know what each instrument was doing, you could always hear Freddie Green. And when you hear all…

I want to ask you, can you delineate for us if I’m having some students that are going to be watching this video. Tell us some differences between, like in terms of your tone quality and of the volume, and maybe even what you do in the left hand, between jazz guitar playing and rock guitar playing. Now I will tell you this. I met a rock guitar player. I was in a music store trying out an instrument and he was in there kind of banging away with big bar chords and stuff. And I told him, you know, you need to listen…
